name: Soybean meal; solvent-extracted; region 4; at soybean processing plant
description: Cradle-to-processing plant gate system boundary for the production of 1000kg soybean oil and the associated amount of soybean meal in the stated region. The allocation of material and energy inputs of oil/soybean meal 80:20. Data are based on 50 of the 60 soybean processing plants that NOPA represents, and are broadly reflective of energy and material inputs and outputs for soybean processing plants similar in general design and processes to the plant that was evaluated in their 1998 Report.

processDocumentation.geographyDescription: The unit process is assumed to represent regional production in Region 4.  US Region 4 including Texas, Oklahoma, Nebraska, Kansas, North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, Idaho, Colorado, Wyoming, Utah, New Mexico, Arizona, and Nevada.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: Cradle-to-processing plant gate system boundary. The allocation of material and energy inputs of soybean meal to soybean oil is based on NOPA Soybean Crushing and Extraction Process soybean oil/soybean meal 80:20.  For more information on this process, visit:  http://www.nescaum.org/documents/stakeholder-comments-on-the-low-carbon-fuels-standard/comments-from-national-biodiesel-board/soybean-processing-documentation1-26-09-nopa-board-revision-030409.pdf/.
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Life cycle inventory was originally assembled using the SimaPro software platform (Version 8.0.4.26) and was modified for submission using the OpenLCA platform (Version 1.3.0).
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: This model includes main resource use and environmnetal impact drivers. Average soybean production regional input for soybean meal and oil production. It excludes soybean hulls. Regional soybean production including Soybeans, region 2, at farm/US U, Soybeans, region 3, at farm/US U, Soybeans, region 4, at farm/US U were modeled by University of Arkansas and it was assumed that average amount of soybean meal from each region is necessary to produce soybean meal and oil and region 1. Industrial land use occupation was adopted from Mila i Canals 2013 Land Use Impact Assessment of Margarine for 1, 000 kg of oil produced.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Data collected from literature. The data that NOPA received were provided as full-facility inputs and outputs on a per-soybean input basis, and cover soybean processing via solvent extraction through crude oil degumming
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: The National Oilseed Processors Association (NOPA) provided inventory for the U.S. industry average of energy and material inputs and products and other outputs. Regional production variations were modeled using soybean produced at particular region. According to NOPA report the mass allocation of soybean meal and soybean oil was done because the economics of soy oil and soy meal values are volatile, requiring data to be updated frequently. We added economic allocation based on ecoinvent soybean model. NOPA’s data, which it obtained by surveying its 15 member companies in mid-December 2008 for data reflective of each company’s most recent fiscal year, do not reflect the performance of any single soybean processing plant. Rather, the data reflect company-applied data that NOPA received on 50 of the 60 soybean processing plants that it represents, and are broadly reflective of energy and material inputs and outputs for soybean processing plants similar in general design and processes to the plant that was evaluated in the 1998 Report.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: NOPA performed sampling from survey data from 15 member companies

reviews.details: University of Arkansas swine dataset mapped to USLCI technosphere flows and FEDEFL elementary flows for publication on the Federal LCA Commons. Review covers mapping crosswalks, cutoff flows, and export structure.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication: These data may be used in Situation C2, “Accounting without interactions.”  This is applicable to accounting studies that according to their goal definition do not include any interaction with other systems.
